prompt: What does the CDK hand to AWS in the end?
hint: The program runs on your machine.

choices.text: The JavaScript program, which AWS runs to create resources
choices.why: AWS never runs your program; it receives what the program printed.

choices.text: A Terraform plan converted to JSON
choices.why: The CDK for AWS targets CloudFormation, not Terraform.

choices.text: A list of API calls the CLI then makes one by one
choices.why: The calls are made by CloudFormation from the template, not by the CLI.

choices.text: A CloudFormation template
choices.why: Right. Synthesis writes a template, and CloudFormation deploys it.

prompt: Match each level of CDK construct to what it is.
hint: From one resource with nothing added, to several services in one call.

pairs.right: A template resource one to one, nothing added
One kind of resource with defaults and named options
An arrangement of several services from one call

right_distractors: A stack deployed in another account

prompt: Why could the CDK version of the log group not repeat the 15-day mistake cfn-lint caught in lesson 4?
hint: Look at how retention is written in app.js.

choices.text: The CDK runs cfn-lint during synthesis
choices.why: It does not; the protection is in the type, before any linter.

choices.text: moto would refuse 15 days at deployment
choices.why: moto refuses very little, and nothing reached it here.

choices.text: Retention is an enumeration
choices.why: Right. logs.RetentionDays has a member per valid period, and 15 is not one.

choices.text: JavaScript does not allow odd numbers in that field
choices.why: Seven days is odd and valid; the list of periods is what matters.

prompt: The app asked for four resources and the template holds a bucket policy as well. Where did it come from?

choices.text: From cdk bootstrap
choices.why: Bootstrapping makes the toolkit stack, not this stack's resources.

choices.text: From enforceSSL: true
choices.why: Right. That one option expands into a full bucket policy.

choices.text: From the alarm's SNS action
choices.why: An alarm action writes AlarmActions, not a bucket policy.

choices.text: From blockPublicAccess
choices.why: That becomes a property of the bucket itself, PublicAccessBlockConfiguration.

prompt: A refactoring moves the `Uploads` construct into a new construct called `Storage`. What will the next change set show for the bucket?
hint: How is the logical id derived?

choices.text: An Add for a new logical id and a Remove for the old one
choices.why: Right. The path, and so the hash, changed; to CloudFormation it is a new bucket.

choices.text: Nothing: the bucket keeps its name, so nothing changes
choices.why: The logical id comes from the path, and the path changed.

choices.text: A Modify with no replacement
choices.why: CloudFormation sees a different logical id, which is a different resource.

choices.text: An error, because the CDK refuses to move constructs
choices.why: The CDK moves them without complaint, which is why the change set must be read.

prompt: The CDK command that runs the program and writes the template, without contacting AWS, is `cdk ___`.
`app.js` had 37 lines and `template.yaml` 84. How many lines did synthesis add beyond the program's own?
What does `cdk bootstrap` create in an account?
hint: What does a deployment need before the template?

choices.text: The application's own stack, created early and ready to update later
choices.why: The application's stack comes from cdk deploy; bootstrap prepares the account.

choices.text: A CDKToolkit stack, with assets storage and roles
choices.why: Right. Deployments upload assets there and assume those roles, and a parameter records the version.

choices.text: A copy of node_modules in S3
choices.why: The library stays on your machine; only the template and assets are uploaded.

choices.text: An IAM user with access keys for the CLI
choices.why: Bootstrap creates roles for deployments, never a user with static keys.

prompt: moto reported `CREATE_COMPLETE` for the CDK stack, but three resources came back as `None`. What is the right conclusion?
hint: Separate what the template says from what a service did.

choices.text: The template is wrong and the policy should be rewritten by hand
choices.why: The template is right; moto skipped resources it does not create.

choices.text: The stack will be complete on AWS too, so nothing needs checking
choices.why: moto's answer says nothing about AWS's; that is the point of the section.

choices.text: The CDK skipped them because the account was not bootstrapped
choices.why: The CDK wrote them into the template; moto did not create them.

choices.text: A status says little: test the template itself
choices.why: Right. moto reported success over what it did not do, so the decisions are tested in the template.

prompt: Before `cdk deploy` executes a change, what does it show and ask about by default?

choices.text: New IAM statements and security group rules
choices.why: Right. Broadening of access is confirmed before the change set runs.

choices.text: Every property of every resource
choices.why: That would be cdk diff in full; deploy asks about the security-relevant part.

choices.text: The monthly cost of the new resources
choices.why: The CDK knows no prices; a cost estimate is a separate tool.

choices.text: Nothing; it executes at once
choices.why: By default it stops on security-relevant changes and asks.

prompt: What does `Template.fromStack` need in order to run?

choices.text: A bootstrapped account
choices.why: Nothing is deployed; no account is involved.

choices.text: Only Node.js and the library
choices.why: Right. It builds the template in memory and checks it there.

choices.text: moto running on port 4567
choices.why: The test calls no API at all.

choices.text: Network access to download the template
choices.why: The template is produced locally from the program.

prompt: `hasResourceProperties` is given only `PolicyDocument.Statement` with one matching statement. The real policy has a second statement too. Does the test pass?

choices.text: No, because the arrays differ in length
choices.why: Match.arrayWith only requires the given items to be present.

choices.text: Only if the second statement is a Deny as well
choices.why: The extra statement's content is not checked at all.

choices.text: It depends on the order of the statements
choices.why: arrayWith finds the items wherever they are.

choices.text: Yes: extra statements and properties are allowed
choices.why: Right. The test pins the decision, not the whole policy.

prompt: Which of these are worth a fine-grained test in the shop's stack? Choose all that apply.
hint: Decisions that are easy to undo and expensive to miss.

choices.text: The bucket refuses plain HTTP
choices.why: Yes. One line removes it, and nothing else would notice.

choices.text: The bucket is kept when the stack is deleted
choices.why: Yes. Losing it loses customers' uploads.

choices.text: The exact hash in the bucket's logical id
choices.why: No. That is what a snapshot pins, and it changes with harmless refactorings.

choices.text: The alarm notifies the topic
choices.why: Yes. An alarm that tells nobody is no alarm.

choices.text: The order of the keys in the template
choices.why: No. The order means nothing to CloudFormation.

prompt: Put the steps from a CDK change to AWS in the order a careful pipeline runs them.
hint: Test what you wrote before anybody sees what it changes.
items: Run the tests on the synthesized template
Synthesize the template in the build
Create a change set from the template
A person approves the change set
trap: Testing after deploying is the slip: the test exists to stop the deployment.

prompt: A library upgrade changes what `enforceSSL` writes. Which practice notices before production does?
hint: The template is where the change shows.

choices.text: Pinning the library forever so it never changes
choices.why: A library frozen for ever misses fixes; the change has to be seen, not avoided.

choices.text: Reading the new template and its change set
choices.why: Right. Plus the fine-grained test, which fails if the decision is lost.

choices.text: Deploying to moto and checking the stack status
choices.why: moto reported complete while skipping the very policy in question.

choices.text: Running cdk bootstrap again
choices.why: Bootstrap prepares the account; it reads nothing of the app's template.
